notes: A.1 item 151 — "RECORD DELIMITER clause (if not specified, method for determining length of variable-length records). This item is required. This item shall be documented in the implementor's user documentation. (12.4.5.11, RECORD DELIMITER clause, General rule 5)" (cite.py --check A.1 OK). The determination is filed in docs/CONFORMANCE.md §7 and the compiler does what it says: a 4-byte little-endian length prefix per record for record sequential, relative and indexed files, the line delimiter for LINE SEQUENTIAL. They are the only two methods this implementation has: the clause's implementor-names select one of them by name (BINARY-SEQUENTIAL the prefix, LINE-SEQUENTIAL the line delimiter; item 150, kb/Work PB5844), and its declined STANDARD-1 phrase leaves the prefix in force (§2 row 26, COBOL1778). Witnessed by golden file F4, the one file in it with no clause, whose 3- and 8-byte records read back at those lengths. retired-witness: src/Cobol.Net.Runtime/IO/RecordFraming.cs#PrefixLength (kb/Work PB2754 made RecordFraming.EncodeFrameHead the one encoder and RecordFraming.ReadFrame the one decoder of the documented 4-byte length prefix, as docs/CONFORMANCE.md DOC-A.1-151 now states; the Latin-1 char decoders, PrefixLength among them, were deleted, and WritePrefix had already been replaced by WriteFrameHead) retired-witness: src/Cobol.Net.Runtime/IO/RecordFraming.cs#WritePrefix (kb/Work PB2754 made RecordFraming.EncodeFrameHead the one encoder and RecordFraming.ReadFrame the one decoder of the documented 4-byte length prefix, as docs/CONFORMANCE.md DOC-A.1-151 now states; the Latin-1 char decoders, PrefixLength among them, were deleted, and WritePrefix had already been replaced by WriteFrameHead)
